duplicates.main_topic: The U.S. canal project succeeded after Gorgas's sanitation campaigns against yellow fever and malaria and Stevens's reorganization of the railroad and excavation work. The article also covers the West Indian laborers who did much of the work and the opening of the canal in August 1914.
